## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Kilocode #12784: Replace chokidar with @parcel/watcher for file watching — preserve atomic saves (MODERATE ~4-6h)

- **What**: Replace chokidar file watcher with @parcel/watcher (native watcher backed by FSEvents/ReadDirectoryChangesW/inotify) for code indexing. Preserves updates after atomic saves (tmp file + rename pattern used by vim, emacs, most editors), directory changes (mkdir/rmdir now trigger re-scans so new subdirectories index immediately), and ignore re-includes (when .gitignore changes to whitelist a previously-ignored path, the watcher picks it up; chokidar's stale ignore cache missed it until restart). Migration: replace chokidar.watch with watcher.subscribe, handle event batching (Parcel fires many granular events vs chokidar's coalesced ones), add unsubscribe on shutdown. @parcel/watcher is already a transitive dependency via other tools (no new install). Supports graceful degradation: falls back to polling when native backends unavailable.
- **Why**: Atomic saves are ubiquitous (every major editor uses tmp+rename for crash safety). Missing these events means the index is stale until manual refresh. Same for directory ops and ignore changes. @parcel/watcher's native backends are faster and more accurate than chokidar's stat-based approach.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/12784 (fix(indexing): replace chokidar file watcher with @parcel/watcher)
- **Category**: tool (if Alexi adds file-watching for config auto-reload) OR config (if applied to existing config reload logic)
- **Size**: MODERATE (~4-6h — Alexi has no code indexing surface yet, so this is NOT immediately actionable. However, if file-watching is added for auto-reloading routing-config.json, mcp-servers.json, .env, or other config files, this is the proven choice. Kilo's PR shows the pattern: replace chokidar.watch → watcher.subscribe, batch events (debounce/throttle), unsubscribe on cleanup. Would also apply to plugin/skill hot-reload if those surfaces are added. Keep on radar for when file-watching enters scope.)

#### 2. Cline #13649: .clineignore enforcement hook example — pattern-based access control (MODERATE ~3-4h)

- **What**: PreToolUse hook script (documented example, not built-in) that blocks read_files, editor, apply_patch, and run_commands tool calls targeting paths matching gitignore-style patterns in a workspace `.clineignore` file, and protects `.clineignore` itself from modification. Works in both CLI (`.cline/hooks/PreToolUse.sh`) and VSCode extension (`.clinerules/hooks/PreToolUse`). Handles both hook payload shapes (stringified JSON in CLI, structured object in VSCode). Lexically canonicalizes paths (collapse `.`, `..`, empty segments) before the ignore match and the .clineignore self-protection check, closing bypasses via noncanonical paths like `./.clineignore`, `secrets/../.env`, `/root/./file`. Returns `{allowed: false, reason: "..."}` when blocked. Replaces the deprecated built-in .clineignore feature (which was removed from Cline core).
- **Why**: Users need pattern-based access control to protect secrets, credentials, and sensitive files from accidental agent reads/edits. The built-in feature was deprecated; this hook-based approach is the official replacement. Path canonicalization hardens against trivial bypasses. Hook model is more flexible (users can customize the patterns, add logging, extend to other tools).
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13649 (docs: add .clineignore hook example)
- **Category**: tool (permission/hook)
- **Size**: MODERATE (~3-4h — Alexi has no .clineignore concept yet. This is a **reference implementation** for pattern-based access control. If a user-facing ignore system is added to Alexi (e.g. `.alexiignore` or `.aiignore`), copy this pattern: (1) PreToolUse hook in `src/hooks/`, (2) gitignore-style parser (use `ignore` npm package, already a dependency in many projects), (3) path canonicalization (`path.normalize` + strip leading `./` + collapse `..`), (4) block read/edit/patch/bash tools targeting matched paths, (5) self-protect the ignore file. Also document it as a user-facing hook example. Keep on radar for when permission hardening enters scope.)

#### 3. Kilocode #13713: Prune old tool outputs in single-turn subagents — context size optimization (LOW priority, specialized)

- **What**: Single-turn subagents (Task tool invocations with background=false) now prune tool outputs from earlier turns (keeps only the most recent turn's outputs) before sending the final message back to the parent. Multi-turn subagents and parents unchanged. Prevents context bloat when a subagent makes many tool calls (e.g. explore agent running 20 grep/read cycles): the parent only receives the subagent's final summary text + the last turn's tool outputs, not the full transcript. Pruning happens in the CLI's subagent response builder, keyed on the single-turn flag.
- **Why**: Single-turn subagents are expected to return a concise answer, not their full work log. Keeping all intermediate outputs wastes the parent's context budget (especially when the parent fans out multiple subagents in parallel).
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13713 (fix(cli): prune old tool outputs in single-turn subagents)
- **Category**: command (subagent response handling)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP — Alexi's subagent implementation (`src/agent/`, `src/core/orchestrator.ts`) does not explicitly distinguish single-turn vs multi-turn (no background= flag, no Task tool yet). If a Task tool is added matching Kilo's API surface, revisit this for context optimization. For now, not immediately applicable.

#### 4. Cline #13785 / #13787: Hub version mismatch prompt hardening — avoid false-positive upgrade loops (LOW priority, desktop/hub-specific)

- **What**: Two PRs hardening the outdated-hub prompt: (1) #13785 never prompts when the hub's coreVersion equals the client's own (even if build fingerprints differ due to separate release cuts from different commits — desktop-v0.0.22 and cli-v3.0.61 both bundle core 0.0.82, but every desktop user with CLI installed got the 'Cline Hub was updated' dialog on every launch, and 'Update and restart' looped on 'no app update available'). (2) #13787 shows the build_mismatch modal only when the auto-updater reports a staged update ('ready'), so it can never loop on 'no app update available yet'; 'Later' now persists in localStorage per reason:hubBuildId (the sidecar replays the mismatch on every webview reconnect, and the previous in-memory dismissal resurrected it each time). unsupported_protocol keeps its unconditional dialog and session-local dismissal.
- **Why**: Release skew (desktop/CLI/hub built from the same core but different git commits) caused false-positive upgrade prompts. Persistence prevents modal resurrection on every reconnect. Protocol-incompatible hubs still prompt unconditionally (correct behavior).
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13785, https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13787
- **Category**: command (hub version negotiation)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP — Alexi is CLI-first, has no hub daemon, no desktop app, no auto-updater. Cline's hub is a separate process (cron runner, session multiplexer) that desktop/CLI clients connect to; Alexi's agent workflows run in GitHub Actions runners (no persistent daemon). Not applicable to Alexi's architecture.

#### 5. Cline #13652 / #13657 / #13658: Hub-managed Agent Plugins support — distributed plugin architecture (HIGH complexity, DEFER)

- **What**: Three PRs implementing Agent Plugins, a new plugin distribution model: plugins are installed/enabled/disabled through the Hub (central daemon), and clients (desktop, CLI) discover them at runtime. Core adds InMemoryMcpManager lifecycle (load manifests from installed plugin dirs, connect stdio MCP clients, expose tools/skills, disconnect on dispose), AgentPluginService (install/uninstall/list/enable/disable/update), and plugin skill toggles (whole-plugin disable persists to Hub storage, per-skill toggles are rejected with an error pointing to the plugin toggle). CLI and desktop add `list`/`install`/`uninstall`/`enable`/`disable` commands backed by Hub RPCs. Plugins carry a strict manifest schema (name, description, license, compatibility, metadata, allowed-tools in SKILL.md frontmatter); extra fields break the parser. Auto-discovery scoped to `~/.cline/plugins/` (no system-wide paths). Stdio MCP processes await full shutdown (close stdin, drain stdout/stderr, wait for exit) so dispose() doesn't leak processes.
- **Why**: Centralized plugin management (one install surfaces in all connected clients). Strict schema + allowlist model improves security vs uncontrolled script loading. Stdio MCP is the standard plugin protocol (Anthropic, OpenAI tools teams converging on it).
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13652, https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13657, https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13658
- **Category**: plugin + mcp
- **Size**: HIGH complexity ~16-20h, DEFER — Alexi already has MCP client support (`src/mcp/`) and plugin loading (`src/plugin/`), but no hub daemon, no centralized install, no desktop UI. Cline's model is desktop/hub-centric (the hub daemon persists across CLI invocations; the desktop app is the primary UI). Alexi is CLI-first, stateless per invocation, with file-based session storage. Agent Plugins would require either (a) a persistent Alexi daemon (large architecture change, out of scope), or (b) replicating the plugin-install surface in the CLI and storing plugin manifests in `~/.alexi/plugins/`, with per-invocation discovery (closer to Alexi's model, but still ~12h for manifest schema, install/uninstall commands, skill frontmatter parser, allowlist enforcement, stdio lifecycle). DEFER until user demand emerges or a hub-like daemon is added.
